title: Hypertension in Adults [Adapted from NICE]
specialty: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine and Cardiology

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with raised blood pressure: confirming the diagnosis, assessing risk and organ damage, lifestyle, stepwise drug treatment, targets, resistant hypertension and same-day referral. Verified against the National Heart Center/Saudi Heart Association 2023 hypertension guideline and NICE NG136; doses from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Single-pill combination products and doses not reproduced
Hypertensive emergency drug doses not covered (see emergency topic)

pathophysiology.summary: Sustained high blood pressure reflects raised vascular resistance, sodium–volume excess and neurohormonal (renin–angiotensin, sympathetic) activation. Chronic pressure load damages the heart, brain, kidneys, eyes and arteries.
keyMechanisms: Arterial stiffening and endothelial dysfunction increase resistance.
RAS activation and salt retention raise volume and vascular tone — targets for ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics.
Organ damage: left ventricular hypertrophy, albuminuria, retinopathy, stroke.

symptoms: Headache, visual change, chest pain or confusion with very high BP suggest emergency.
physicalSigns: BP both arms (repeat if difference over 15 mmHg) (NICE 1.2.1); fundi; signs of heart failure; secondary-cause clues.
redFlags: BP 180/120 or more with retinal haemorrhage/papilloedema or life-threatening symptoms — same-day referral (NICE 1.5.2)
BP 180/120 or more without symptoms — test for organ damage urgently (NICE 1.5.1)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Young age, resistant BP, hypokalaemia, renal disease — specialist (NICE 1.4.14).
Ask; SHA advises avoiding excess licorice.

ruleIn.testName: Clinic BP with ABPM or HBPM confirmation
ruleIn.expectedFinding: SHA: 130/80 or more diagnoses hypertension; treatment considered at 140/90 clinic or 135/85 home. NICE: confirm with ABPM/HBPM 135/85 or more.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and assess
actions: Repeat clinic readings; confirm with ABPM (or HBPM) (NICE 1.2.3–1.2.8).
Screen adults at every visit where feasible; yearly from 40 or with risk factors (SHA Table 4).
Organ damage tests and cardiovascular risk while confirming (NICE 1.2.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Lifestyle for all
actions: Salt to 2–4 g/day maximum, more fruit and vegetables, 30 minutes moderate exercise 5–7 days a week, stop tobacco, weight control, limit sugar-sweetened drinks and licorice (SHA).

clinicalManagement.title: Drug treatment
actions: SHA: single-pill combination (RAS blocker with CCB or diuretic) as initial therapy for most; monotherapy for low-risk stage 1 with SBP below 150, very high risk with elevated BP, or frail older people.
NICE step 1: ACE inhibitor or ARB if diabetes or under 55; CCB if 55 or over without diabetes.
Step 2: add CCB or thiazide-like diuretic; step 3: ACEi/ARB + CCB + thiazide-like diuretic (NICE 1.4.41–1.4.45; SHA Table 10).
Never combine ACE inhibitor with ARB (NICE 1.4.34).

clinicalManagement.title: Resistant hypertension
actions: Confirm with ABPM/HBPM, check adherence and postural BP (NICE 1.4.47).
Low-dose spironolactone if K+ 4.5 mmol/L or less; alpha- or beta-blocker if K+ above 4.5 (NICE 1.4.49–1.4.51; SHA).
Check sodium, potassium and renal function within 1 month (NICE 1.4.50).
Specialist referral if still uncontrolled (NICE 1.4.52; SHA).

learningObjectives: Confirm, assess and treat hypertension to target.

keyPoints: Lifestyle for everyone; limit salt and licorice.
SHA: start with a single-pill combination for most.

patientEducation: Home BP technique; adherence; salt reduction.
lifestyleAndDiet: Salt 2–4 g/day maximum; 30 min exercise 5–7 days a week; weight control; stop tobacco.
mdtReferrals: Specialist for resistant or secondary hypertension, or under 40.
dischargeCriteria: Not applicable — outpatient care unless hypertensive emergency.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: SHA: review 1–2 months after starting or changing treatment; every 3–6 months once controlled. NICE: annual review. Targets: NICE below 140/90 (under 80) or 150/90 (80 and over); SHA: below 130/80 in diabetes.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 180/120 with retinal changes or life-threatening symptoms
